subject: Private offer timeline and legal signoff — BrightChat capacity increase
messages:
From: Lila Gomez <lila@brightchat.ai>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: Aaron Chen <aaron.chen@brightchat.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity bump + timeline for AWS private offer

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for last week's demo — the infra team is comfortable and the execs are aligned to move forward with a quarterly capacity increase. We want to move to a private offer on AWS for predictable billing and the reserved pricing you quoted. High level asks:

- Add 2 additional Dedicated GPU units (estimate ~300M tokens/mo)
- Annual term, prefer Apr 1 start date
- Need PO + marketplace private offer paperwork signed by Apr 5 so procurement can submit payment on time

Can you confirm Redwood can deliver the PO and private-offer doc by EOD Apr 1? Also, are there any commercial constraints that might push the start date out?

Attaching our internal forecast for capacity.

Thanks,
Lila Gomez
Head of Partnerships, BrightChat
Attachment: BrightChat_capacity_forecast.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: Lila Gomez <lila@brightchat.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity bump + timeline for AWS private offer

Lila — appreciate the clear timeline. Internal plan below.

Summary / ask: We can do Apr 1 start provided legal signoff + PO are completed by Apr 4 and the AWS private offer is submitted Apr 5 at the latest. I'll coordinate with Marissa (Marketplace/Finance) and Rafael (Legal) for redlines and DocuSign.

Mutual Action Plan (short):
- 3/11: Redwood issues draft PO and fills AWS Private Offer template (PR) — Priyom
- 3/12–3/18: Internal review (Marissa/Rafael) and 1 cycle of redlines/clarifications
- 3/19: Final PO and private-offer package prepared for signing
- 3/20: DocuSign out to BrightChat execs
- 4/1: Contract effective date (customer billing calendar begins)

I attached a first-pass PO (BrightChat_PO_v2.pdf) and the AWS template we plan to populate. Can Marissa confirm whether billing team needs a consolidated invoice schedule (monthly vs. quarterly) for the PO? Rafael — are there any legal flags we should flag to the customer now (IP, data residency, SLA exceptions)?

Thanks — Priyom
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: BrightChat_PO_v2.pdf (PDF stub), AWS_Private_Offer_Template.docx (docx stub)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: rafael_mendes@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 08:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity bump + timeline for AWS private offer

Priyom — quick notes from finance/marketplace side after a pass on the PO and template:

1) Billing cadence: BrightChat should pick monthly invoicing for predictable cashflow. If they elect quarterly, collections team requires NET30 on quarter close — that pushes our need for PO by Apr 1. Recommend we propose monthly in the DocuSign schedule and call out the option to switch to quarterly with 30 days notice.

2) Marketplace SKU mapping: I'll need the exact SKU mapping (region + instance type) from the infra team. Karhtik — can you confirm whether the Dedicated GPU SKU for this offer will be the same SKU we used last quarter or a new SKU?

3) Marketplace private offer timing: AWS needs the Private Offer request submitted to the marketplace console and countersigned by both parties. Realistically, allow 3 business days after we push final docs for AWS processing. That means our internal signoff needs to be no later than Mar 23 to safely hit Apr 1.

Rafael — please flag any legal redlines; if none major, I can prepare the invoice schedule and marketplace submission.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Finance Operations, Redwood Inference

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
To: priyom_das@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity bump + timeline for AWS private offer

Looping back after legal review — short version: good to go with two minor edits. See inline notes and next steps below.

Legal redlines (high level):
- Limitation of liability: remove carve-out for derived data in section 7.2; replace with standard cap at 1x annual fees for the PO term.
- Data residency: customer requested EU-only residency for a portion of usage. We can't promise region-restricted inference on Dedicated without a region-specific deployment. Add language that we will provide best-effort routing and document the subset of traffic covered; recommend keeping billing on US terms for this PO and follow up on a private deployment conversation.

Next steps:
- I attached a marked-up PO (BrightChat_PO_v2_marked.pdf) — we should present these two changes to BrightChat during the signature cycle.
- Marissa: once redlines are agreed, I can sign via DocuSign on Redwood's side.
- Priyom: confirm whether BrightChat is OK with the proposed limitation cap and the routing language; if they insist on hard guarantees for EU residency we'll need a separate SOW and timeline.

I'll be online tomorrow morning to review the final DocuSign packet.

Rafael Mendes
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: BrightChat_PO_v2_marked.pdf (PDF markup stub)
